penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: OST-to-PST conversion and data validation is a technical file-processing task requiring local software execution against proprietary binary file formats. It cannot be delivered as a Claude API call or a web form—actual conversion tooling (Stellar, Kernel, etc.) must run locally on the customer's machine or on a server with the file. Each recovery job is a per-customer manual or semi-manual operation.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: Data recovery engagements typically require back-and-forth with the customer to scope the file, validate recovered items, handle corruption edge cases, and confirm compliance requirements are met—this is not async automated delivery.

rationale: IT admins at SMBs and enterprises are a legitimate, budget-holding buyer segment, and the paid tool market (Stellar, Kernel) confirms willingness to pay for OST recovery. However, the core technical constraint is fatal for this factory: OST is a proprietary Microsoft binary format, and actual file conversion requires specialized local software—not a Claude prompt or a web API. Operational autonomy scores 2 because every job requires direct file handling, and buildability scores 3 because no combination of Claude + standard tooling can process binary OST files. After penalties the total is 2.5; this is definitively a drop.
solution_plan: This opportunity is NOT buildable by a solo non-technical operator using this factory. OST-to-PST conversion requires proprietary format parsing software that must run locally (or on a controlled server) against the customer's actual binary file—Claude cannot read, parse, or convert OST files. The existing paid incumbents (Stellar Phoenix, Kernel for OST) are specialized software products built by technical teams with deep knowledge of Microsoft's undocumented file formats. A 'guide' or 'checklist' service (what steps to follow) has near-zero willingness to pay since free information already exists on ServerFault and Microsoft docs. Recommending drop.
notes: Fails operational_autonomy build gate (scored 2, floor is 7) and buildability_with_ai build gate (scored 3, floor is 6). Weighted total of 5.0 is below the 5.5 validate threshold before penalties are even applied. Drop is correct.
